title: Come, Let Us, Who in Christ Believe
description: Come, Let Us, Who in Christ Believe in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 208. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, let us, who in Christ be-lieve, Our com-mon Sa-viour praise, To him with joy-ful voi-ces give The glo-ry of his grace.

lines: Come, let us, who in Christ believe,
To him with joyful voices give
He now stands knocking at the door
The worst need keep him out no more,
Through grace we hearken to thy voice,
Yield to be saved from sin;
In sure and certain hope rejoice,
Come quickly in, thou heavenly guest,
But sup with us, and let the feast

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
